title: Spatiotemporal Pattern Evolution and Driving Mechanisms of World Botanical Gardens Over Five Centuries
content:
This study presents a comprehensive review of the 500-year spatiotemporal evolution of global botanical gardens, identifying three major development stages—initial exploration (1543–1699), steady expansion (1700–1899), and rapid proliferation (1900–2020)—with six distinct sub-stages. We propose a tripartite driving framework grounded in colonial botany and world-systems theory: civilizational progress as the material foundation, cultural–scientific–commercial demands as functional drivers, and the global conservation movement as the modern normative driver. Colonial commercial imperatives decisively shaped the 19th-century transcontinental diffusion of gardens, leaving a lasting core-periphery legacy in the contemporary global spatial pattern. Six forward-looking recommendations are offered to guide the future high-quality development of botanical gardens worldwide.


ABSTRACT

Botanical gardens are the main means of ex situ conservation of biodiversity. The world's first botanical garden with modern significance was established in Italy in 1543, and since then, the proliferation of these institutions has exhibited clear spatiotemporal patterns. Based on a systematic review of the literature, the present paper divides these temporal and spatial aspects of botanical garden development over the past 500 years into three major phases: the initial exploration stage (1543–1699), the steady development stage (1700–1899), and the rapid development stage (1900–2020). Six distinct sub-stages are identified and examined. Furthermore, while scrutinizing the progression and achievements of each stage, we discerned three driving mechanisms for the rise, dissemination, development, and evolution of botanical gardens: human civilization and progress; culture, health, science, and education; and the world nature conservation movement. These findings are expected to serve as a valuable reference point for the ongoing construction, management, and practice of botanical gardens. A series of recommendations is also proposed to support these endeavors.

摘要

植物园是生物多样性迁地保护的主要载体。世界上第一座具有现代意义的植物园于1543年成立于意大利, 此后五百余年间, 植物园的数量增长呈现出明显的时空演变特征。本文基于系统文献综述, 将过去500年全球植物园的发展划分为三个主要阶段:初步探索阶段 (1543–1699年) 、稳步发展阶段 (1700–1899年) 和快速发展阶段 (1900–2020年), 并进一步识别和分析了六个子阶段。在此基础上, 本文提炼出驱动植物园兴起、传播与演化的三重机制:人类文明进步作为物质基础, 文化, 健康, 科学, 教育与商业殖民需求交织作为功能引擎, 以及全球自然保护运动作为现代规范导向。其中, 殖民时期的商业与帝国扩张需求在19世纪植物园的跨洲扩散中发挥了决定性作用, 并深刻塑造了当今全球植物园空间格局中核心—边缘的不均衡分布。本文还提出了六条建议, 以期为全球植物园的未来建设、管理与实践提供参考。
